$comment: §4.1 — the Intent a play emits (controller class) and the standing order the body executes. Canonical rules: schemas/README.md. Caps: reason ≤ 64 bytes; whole encoding well under MaxEmitBytes (4096).
title: intent

point.$comment: REQUIRED iff kind is navigate_to; forbidden for hold (schema rejection either way, §6.1). Map pixels, inside map bounds; the engine validates and may NORMALIZE it via nearestReachable at emit (§6.1), and the accepted canonical bytes carry the returned point.

micro.$comment: SET kind: sorted, deduplicated; omit when empty. Stencil's permission set minus the deleted pursuit flag (§3.3).

idle_aim_center_brads.$comment: omit when unset; the finisher stamps it if absent (§7.3)

clamp_to_endzone.$comment: omit when false; meaningful in ctf only, ignored elsewhere

handoff.$comment: omit when absent (neutral). §4.1 amendment (owner spec 2026-09-02): the STANDING give-item declaration; valid only in mode br (a duo fact, rejected elsewhere exactly like duo: references). The target is deliberately NOT a field — it is always the duo partner, resolved by the engine at execution through the sim.declareHandoff consent seam. The vocabulary is that seam's own.

target_class.$comment: omit when absent (neutral). NAVCLASS (owner ruling 2026-09-04): valid only with kind navigate_to. Names a CLASS the engine re-resolves and navigates to every tick instead of a fixed point. `point` stays REQUIRED and becomes the fallback the engine uses on any tick the class cannot be resolved -- an unresolvable class with no fallback would leave the seat with no goal, and a seat with no goal stands still (the round-3633 death). The vocabulary is CLOSED on purpose: the membership check IS the integrity check, and the moment it admits a free-form expression the engine starts making strategic choices. The play still decides whether to pursue and which class; what leaves is the arithmetic (a Euclidean argmin through walls, or a bearing to a zone rectangle that does not describe the damage). Item classes are deliberately absent: a shared item field would leak crates a seat has never seen into a fogged view.

reason.$comment: telemetry only; omit when empty; the cap is UTF-8 BYTES, engine-enforced (maxLength counts code points and is deliberately not used)

combat.$comment: omit when neutral (everything empty/false). On the standing order this is the FOLDED policy (§7.1); on a controller emission it is the play's own.
